findings.text: Two routines cooperate to return interrupt delivery to firmware expectations. The low level form programs the remembered cascade pin with an unmasked edge triggered high polarity physical destination external interrupt entry aimed at the boot processor when a valid pin was recorded, then conditionally detaches the bootstrap local unit. The public form is a no operation when the platform reports no legacy inputs and otherwise forwards to the configured restore operation.

Early initialization establishes identifiers, mappings, resources and allocation bounds. Identifier setup from firmware tables is skipped when ACPI owns the units or when vendor and version checks indicate no serial bus meaning. Mapping creates one fixed entry per unit and records a busy memory extent for each, with a fallback anonymous page when firmware configuration is absent. A separate step inserts those extents into the global memory tree. A bound helper returns the initialized dynamic base or the GSI top, falling back to the caller start when both are zero for device tree or empty cases.

Two vector layer helpers support migration and acknowledgement. Completion checks a per data move flag and, when the current processor matches the new target, arranges cleanup of the previous vector. Acknowledgement advances any pending move before issuing the local end of interrupt signal, and is used on remapped level paths before pin specific completion.

Diagnostic reporting walks all units and active interrupt numbers. It prints per unit register counts and redirection contents, then for each active number that is served by either IOAPIC chip variant and has associated pin state with a non empty pin list, it emits the interrupt number followed by its apic and pin pairs.

Identifier assignment enforces uniqueness across local and IO units. A reserved broadcast value is rejected and replaced by the hardware reported value with a firmware report. Collisions against the processor presence set are resolved by scanning for the first free value below broadcast, aborting when none remains, updating the firmware table copy and rewriting any IRQ routing entries that referenced the old value. The hardware identifier register is rewritten only when it differs, then reread and checked with a failure notice on mismatch.

Several paths gate behavior on platform properties. Identifier setup is bypassed for ACPI owned units and for non Intel or xAPIC parts. Boot mode restoration is bypassed when no legacy inputs exist and conditionally touches the bootstrap unit based on capability or configuration presence. Dynamic bound selection treats zero base and zero top as invalid and substitutes the caller value for device tree or unit less systems.

Startup for an IOAPIC interrupt holds the central lock, and for legacy numbers first masks through the legacy controller and samples whether one was pending. It then unmasks the hardware entry and returns the pending indication so the core can handle an already asserted line.

Level state is derived from the remote receiver indicator. A scan helper reports pending acknowledgement when any associated pin shows the indicator set in its low routing word. The chip state query only supports the active query, fails other kinds, and reports active only when some pin shows both the indicator and level mode, ignoring the indicator for edge mode as undefined fire and forget.

Remapped entries are composed from the parent message and then fanned out. Vector, delivery, destination mode, format and index portions are transferred from message address and data portions into the cached entry, covering real vectors, subhandles and destination identifier extension cases. Configuration writes the cached entry to every associated pin. Affinity first delegates to the parent and, under lock, reconfigures only on success codes other than fully handled.

Dynamic lower bound and trigger polarity resolution use ordered fallbacks. The bound prefers the initialized base, else the GSI top, else the caller start. Polarity and level come first from explicit allocation info when valid, else from an ACPI override lookup, else default to active low level for PCI.

Resource descriptors are allocated as one contiguous early block holding an array plus trailing name storage. Each unit gets a busy memory typed entry named with its index, sized to one slot. Mapping fills start and end from the firmware address or fallback page, and insertion adds each entry to the global tree with an error note when allocation never happened but units exist.

The ioapic_lock serializes register and entry changes. It covers identifier register reads and writes during early setup and resume, startup masking and unmasking, remote indicator scans, affinity reconfiguration, active state queries and pin entry programming. Early setup uses scoped acquisition for single reads and for write plus reread sequences, while other paths hold across the whole critical section including legacy controller interaction.

The vector_lock serializes migration cleanup state. It protects clearing of the move flag, queueing onto the previous processor cleanup list, timer expiry update and arming, plus immediate release when that processor is offline. The timer pending test, list add and arming are performed atomically so callbacks and concurrent schedulers observe consistent state.

Three chip descriptors expose operation sets. Both IOAPIC variants share state query, hierarchy retrigger, affinity, parent acknowledgement, unmask, mask and startup, differing only in end of interrupt handling for plain versus remapped level paths and in flags for deferred moves. The plain variant allows deferred moves and pre startup affinity while skipping wake, the remapped variant skips wake and allows pre startup affinity without deferral. The local variant offers only mask, unmask and end of interrupt against the local vector zero register.

Boot routing, sentinel storage and power hooks form a small state group. The ioapic_i8259 tracker holds a pin and apic pair initialized to negative one meaning none recorded. Boot programming uses cleared storage with selected fields set for unmasked edge high physical external interrupt toward the boot identifier split across low and high portions. Power suspend saves entries, resume restores identifiers in reverse order then restores entries, wired through an ops pair and a registered core object created at init.

Affinity migration follows a prepare and finish pair with two builds. The active build masks when a move is pending and core state is unmasked, returning whether migration work remains. Its finish migrates only when no remote acknowledgement is pending, then restores unmasked state when the core is unmasked. The alternate build is inert, always reporting no work and doing nothing on finish.

Vector cleanup moves through completion to scheduled release. Completion is a no operation without a move flag, otherwise it schedules when on the new processor. Scheduling clears the flag under lock, and for an online previous processor queues onto its per processor list and arms a short timer when not already pending, else warns and releases immediately. Release frees the previous vector, marks its slot unused, unlinks the queue node and clears move state.

Plain level acknowledgement orders move completion, masking, end of interrupt and conditional migration. After completing any move and preparing, it samples the trigger mode state for the assigned vector, issues the local end of interrupt, and when the hardware shows edge for a level interrupt it counts a misroute and performs pin level completion to clear the remote state. It then finishes any pending move.

Remapped level acknowledgement uses the pin number as the virtual vector for completion. It advances the move and issues the local end of interrupt through the shared acknowledgement helper, then completes the pin using the cached entry vector and chip data.

Power transitions preserve identifiers and entries. Suspend returns the result of saving all entries. Resume walks units in reverse restoring any identifier that drifted, then restores all entries. The pair is published as suspend and resume callbacks in a static ops object referenced by a static core object registered during early init.

Mapping initialization iterates units with a rising fixed index. With firmware configuration it uses the table address, treating zero as bogus on thirty two bit by disabling IOAPIC support and falling back to an allocated page. Without configuration it always allocates a zeroed page and translates to physical. Each address is installed into the fixed map and logged, with resource extents filled when allocation succeeded.

Boot and driver entry points include two command line switches, a power registration and chip callbacks. One switch enables skipping of timer verification, the other records disabling of timer pin one, both during early parsing. Init registers the power core object. Chip startup handles legacy pending as above, affinity delegates then reconfigures, and state query implements active detection.

Firmware and allocation faults are reported without silent correction. Invalid broadcast identifiers and collisions emit vendor reports and are fixed up, with exhaustion aborting boot. Identifier register write mismatch and missing resource allocation with present units emit error notes. A bogus zero table address on thirty two bit disables IOAPIC support and uses a fake page.

Two interrupt loss hazards shape the code. Reprogramming a vector while remote state remains set can silence a level line forever, so migration is deferred until no acknowledgement is pending and reads are used to flush posted writes. A chipset erratum and offline forwarding can present level as edge, requiring explicit pin completion or edge to level toggling under mask plus a misroute count, with cleanup for offline targets warning and freeing immediately.

Three small constants govern identity, naming and legacy masking. The broadcast identifier value is fifteen and bounds all scans. The resource name buffer length is eleven including terminator. The legacy cascade mask is a single bit shifted by the cascade line number.

Register layout facts include identifier, routing low word, trigger mode and local mask positions. Register zero carries the physical identifier. The low routing word for a pin lives at base sixteen plus twice the pin number and carries the remote indicator. Trigger mode for a vector is sampled from a word chosen by high vector bits with the low five bits selecting the bit. Local mask control toggles the masked bit in the local vector zero register.
